media:group.media:title: He Said 'Fully Booked' Is a Red Flag'. I Kinda Agree.
The 30-Minute Haircut Lie
media:group.media:description:
Barber burnout isn't caused by 30-minute appointments, it's caused by a lack of structure. In this video, I break down why switching to 45-minute blocks is a trap that will cost you 33% of your income without solving the real problem.
After nine years behind the chair, you shouldn't be burned out; you should be working less and making more. The problem isn't the duration of your cuts, it's the system you're running them in. Hustling inside a broken system just gets you to the ceiling faster.
We'll cover the three things you must lock in to fix this for good: 1. Structure: The architecture around your cuts that prevents chaos. 2. Pricing Power: How to raise your prices intelligently so you can work less. 3. Scheduled Recovery: Building vacations and rest into your year to prevent burnout before it starts.
Swinging a dull ax harder won't help. It's time to sharpen the system.

entry.title: Why Taking An Hour Per Haircut Is Keeping You Broke

media:group.media:title: Why Taking An Hour Per Haircut Is Keeping You Broke
media:group.media:description:
One of the easiest ways to make more money as a barber isn't getting faster it's getting efficient. Rushing through haircuts ruins the experience, but taking a full hour per client is going to keep you broke.
In this episode, I break down the "4-Minute Mile" mindset shift that changed my entire career. I went from falling behind on every cut to easily clearing 20-25 haircuts a day while staying perfectly on schedule. I’m also pulling back the curtain on how to systematically break down a 30-minute block so you finish 80% of the cut in the first 20 minutes, leaving you 10 full minutes to refine the details without the client ever feeling rushed. If you want to stop trading time for money and start running your chair like a real business, watch this breakdown.

entry.title: Why Your "Commission" Model is Actually Tax Fraud

media:group.media:title: Why Your "Commission" Model is Actually Tax Fraud
media:group.media:description:
Most barbershop owners want the control of a W2 employee, but the tax break of a 1099 independent contractor. That’s called misclassification, and if your state or the IRS audits you, it will wipe out everything you’ve built.
If you are dictating hours, setting prices, or mandating dress codes for barbers you pay on a 1099, you are running a fake commission model. In this episode, I break down the cold math and legalities of shop models, the ABC Test versus the 14-Point Test, and the true cost of barber churn over a 5-to-10 year time horizon.
Stop building businesses where one side has to lose for the other to win.
